title: The E Sound at the End
kidRule: When a longer word ends with the 'ee' sound, it is usually spelled with just Y, like library. A small group of words use EY instead, like journey and turkey, and those are worth learning by heart.
hint: Listen to the very last sound. It says 'ee', but a plain E almost never does that job at the end of a word like this. Which ending does this word use?
reminder: The 'ee' sound at the end is usually spelled with Y, and a small group of words use E-Y.

check.question: Why does LIBRARY end with the letter Y?
check.correctAnswer: At the end of a longer word, the 'ee' sound is usually spelled with Y!
distractors: Because Y always has to come after the letter R
Because the letter E is too shy to be in this word

words.def: A place full of books that you can borrow and read.
words.sent: We borrowed six books from the library.
words.story: Some libraries lend out much more than books: you can borrow seeds, tools, and even telescopes!
words.card: A *rar*e dragon tiptoed into the *library* to borrow a cookbook!

words.def: A long trip from one place to another.
words.sent: The journey to Grandma's house took all day.
words.story: Monarch butterflies make a journey of thousands of miles to spend the winter in Mexico!
words.card: *Our* snail took a three-day *journey* across the picnic blanket!

words.def: A group of people who belong together, like parents, children, and grandparents.
words.story: A family of lions is called a pride!
words.card: My *family* eats j*am* toast on the trampoline!

words.def: A big bird with a fan-shaped tail that says gobble-gobble.
words.sent: A wild turkey strutted across the road.
words.story: Wild turkeys can fly, and they sleep up in trees at night!
words.card: The *turkey* swallowed the car *key* and gobbled all the way home!

words.def: Something strange that nobody has been able to explain yet.
words.sent: Who ate the last cupcake is still a mystery.
words.story: A writer named Agatha Christie wrote more than 60 mystery books about detectives solving puzzles!
words.card: It is a *mystery* who put jelly in *my* shoes!

words.def: A streetcar that rides along rails in a city street.
words.sent: We rode the trolley up the steep hill.
words.story: San Francisco's famous cable cars are pulled up the hills by a moving cable hidden under the street!
words.card: A grumpy *troll* drove the *trolley* and rang the bell all day!

words.def: The low land between hills or mountains.
words.sent: A river runs through the green valley.
words.story: Many valleys were carved by rivers that slowly wore away the rock over millions of years!
words.card: We *all* rolled down into the *valley* like meatballs!

words.sent: That oak tree has stood for more than a century.
words.story: Some giant tortoises live for more than a hundred years!
words.card: The tortoise saved one *cent* every year for a whole *century*!

words.def: A tall pipe on a roof that lets smoke out of a house.
words.sent: Smoke puffed out of the chimney.
words.story: Little birds called chimney swifts like to sleep inside chimneys, clinging to the walls!
words.card: The squirrel told *him* not to sneeze in the *chimney*!

words.def: Pretty things to wear, like rings, necklaces, and bracelets.
words.sent: The queen kept her jewelry in a velvet box.
words.story: People have been making jewelry for a very long time: some shell beads are tens of thousands of years old!
words.card: The raccoon wore every *jewel* in the *jewelry* box at once!
